question_text:
A researcher is studying how electrical activity propagates across the heart. In order to do this, he decides to measure the rate at which an action potential moves within various groups of cardiac muscle tissue. In particular, he isolates fibers from areas of the heart with the following characteristics:

A) Dysfunction leads to fixed PR intervals prior to a dropped beat
B) Dysfunction leads to increasing PR intervals prior to a dropped beat
C) Dysfunction leads to tachycardia with a dramatically widened QRS complex
D) Dysfunction leads to tachycardia with a sawtooth pattern on electrocardiogram

Which of the following is the proper order of these tissues from fastest action potential propagation to slowest action potential propagation.?

            ### Question
            A researcher is studying how electrical activity propagates across the heart. In order to do this, he decides to measure the rate at which an action potential moves within various groups of cardiac muscle tissue. In particular, he isolates fibers from areas of the heart with the following characteristics:

A) Dysfunction leads to fixed PR intervals prior to a dropped beat
B) Dysfunction leads to increasing PR intervals prior to a dropped beat
C) Dysfunction leads to tachycardia with a dramatically widened QRS complex
D) Dysfunction leads to tachycardia with a sawtooth pattern on electrocardiogram

Which of the following is the proper order of these tissues from fastest action potential propagation to slowest action potential propagation.?

            ### Options
    opa. A > C > D > B
opb. A > D > C > B
opc. B > C > D > A
opd. B > D > C > A
ope. D > C > A > B

            ### Instructions:
            - Keep steps simple, each step just one state or outcome.
            - '->' separates each step.

            ### Output Format:
            Start each chain with "CHAIN:" on a new line.
            Example:
            CHAIN: "Insulin" -> "decreased blood glucose" -> "improved metabolic state" -> 90%

response:
CHAIN: "A: Fixed PR intervals before dropped beat" -> "Indicative of Mobitz Type I (Wenckebach) block" -> "Occurs in AV node" -> "AV node has slower conduction speed compared to ventricles and atria" -> "Slowest action potential propagation" -> 80%

CHAIN: "B: Increasing PR intervals before dropped beat" -> "Indicative of Mobitz Type II block" -> "Occurs in His-Purkinje system" -> "Faster conduction than AV node but slower than normal ventricular tissue" -> "Second slowest action potential propagation" -> 85%

CHAIN: "C: Tachycardia with widened QRS complex" -> "Suggests ventricular tachycardia" -> "Occurs in ventricles" -> "Ventricles have faster conduction than AV node and His-Purkinje system" -> "Second fastest action potential propagation" -> 90%

CHAIN: "D: Tachycardia with sawtooth pattern on ECG" -> "Indicative of atrial flutter" -> "Occurs in atria" -> "Atria have the fastest conduction speed among listed options" -> "Fastest action potential propagation" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Order of propagation speed" -> "D (atria) > C (ventricles) > B (His-Purkinje system) > A (AV node)" -> "Correct order from fastest to slowest" -> 95%
